codes.meaning: A mark for using a correct method, even if the numbers that come out of it are wrong.
codes.source: CCEA Mathematics mark-scheme key ('M indicates marks for correct method'), Summer 2025 M4 MS p.2; counts from the 152-scheme corpus scan 2026-09-05

codes.meaning: A mark for accurate working, a correct reading from a table or graph, or a correct answer. It can only be earned after the method mark it belongs to; a wrong method earns nothing, so M0 A1 is impossible.
codes.source: CCEA Mathematics mark-scheme key ('A indicates marks for accurate working ... M0 A1 cannot be awarded'), Summer 2025 M4 MS p.2; counts from the corpus scan 2026-09-05

codes.meaning: One mark that covers both the method and the accurate result of a single step (used where the step is the method).
codes.source: CCEA Mathematics mark-scheme key ('MA indicates marks for combined method and accurate working'), Summer 2025 M4 MS p.2; counts from the corpus scan 2026-09-05

rules.text: The published scheme shows the most common route to the answer; any other valid route is credited by the examiners, mark for mark, even though it is not printed.
rules.source: CCEA General Marking Instructions (Introduction), Summer 2025 M4 MS

rules.text: An accuracy mark cannot be given without the method mark it follows: if the method is wrong, nothing is awarded for that step.
rules.source: CCEA Mathematics mark-scheme key, Summer 2025 M4 MS

rules.text: If an early slip is carried into later working, the later working is marked using the candidate's own (wrong) value. A candidate who then applies correct method loses only the mark for the original slip. Two or more slips are handled the same way.
rules.source: CCEA General Marking Instructions (follow-through marking), Summer 2025 M4 MS

rules.text: Examiners credit whatever relevant knowledge, skill or understanding is shown: one wrong entry in a table of values that spoils several plotted points counts as one error, and readings taken from a wrongly drawn graph are marked against that graph.
rules.source: CCEA General Marking Instructions (Positive marking), Summer 2025 M4 MS

rules.text: A misread that makes the question easier than intended earns only a proportion of the marks, at the examining team's discretion.
rules.source: CCEA General Marking Instructions, Summer 2025 M4 MS

rules.text: Correct answer in the working, but a plain copying slip on the answer line: full marks.
rules.source: CCEA General Marking Advice (i), Summer 2025 M4 MS

rules.text: Answer line left empty but the correct answer appears in the working: full marks.
rules.source: CCEA General Marking Advice (ii), Summer 2025 M4 MS

rules.text: Correct answer in the working but a genuinely different answer on the answer line: some marks, depending on how serious the difference is.
rules.source: CCEA General Marking Advice (iii), Summer 2025 M4 MS

rules.text: Work that has been crossed out but not replaced by anything else is still marked.
rules.source: CCEA General Marking Advice (iv), Summer 2025 M4 MS

rules.text: If more than one method is offered, only the one that leads to the answer on the answer line is marked. If more than one answer is offered and the answer line is empty, the poorest answer is the one marked.
rules.source: CCEA General Marking Advice (v), Summer 2025 M4 MS

rules.text: A method the scheme did not anticipate is given the equivalent marks for equivalent work.
rules.source: CCEA General Marking Advice (vi), Summer 2025 M4 MS

rules.text: Where a part carries a follow-through mark, the examiner checks back to the candidate's answer to the earlier part before awarding it.
rules.source: CCEA General Marking Advice (vii), Summer 2025 M4 MS

rules.text: Unless the question demands a particular accuracy, the answer is marked at the most significant figures seen anywhere in the response: a fully accurate value in the working followed by a rounded answer on the line still gets full marks.
rules.source: CCEA General Marking Advice (viii), Summer 2025 M4 MS

rules.text: Anything the scheme shows in round brackets is optional for the mark, but if the candidate writes it, it must be right.
rules.source: CCEA General Marking Advice (ix), Summer 2025 M4 MS

rules.text: Any range of acceptable answers printed in the scheme includes both end values.
rules.source: CCEA General Marking Advice (x), Summer 2025 M4 MS

feedbackTemplates.M0: No method mark: {reason}. With no valid method there is no accuracy mark to follow (CCEA: M0 A1 cannot be awarded).
feedbackTemplates.A0: Method mark earned but the accuracy mark is lost — {reason}.
feedbackTemplates.MA0: This step is one combined mark for method and accuracy, and it is lost — {reason}.
feedbackTemplates.ft: Follow-through applied: your value {value} from part {part} was carried forward, so this part is marked on your own working and you lose only the original slip.
feedbackTemplates.answer-line-poorest: Two answers with nothing on the answer line: CCEA marks the poorer one, so {poorer} is what counts. Cross out what you do not want.
feedbackTemplates.sig-figs: You rounded to {given} but the scheme marks at the most accurate figure seen; keep {full} in the working and you keep the mark.
feedbackTemplates.accuracy-demanded: The question asked for {demanded}; {given} does not meet it, so the final accuracy mark is lost.
feedbackTemplates.misread: You read {misread} instead of {intended}; that makes the question easier, so only part of the credit is available.
